text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and the onset of jaundice, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis. Have you noticed any dark urine, pale stools, or fever over the last week? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Serology Panel, Liver Function Tests, CBC.

text: RESULTS: Temperature: 37.0°C (98.6°F); Blood Pressure: 110/60 mm Hg; Heart Rate: 94/min; Respiratory Rate: 13/min. Neurological: Not oriented to time and space; asterixis present. Skin: Jaundice observed. ENT: Epistaxis noted. Blood Work: Hemoglobin 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit 47%, Leukocyte Count 9,750/mm3, Platelet Count 365,000/mm3. Liver Function: Bilirubin 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT 650 IU/L (elevated), TP Activity < 40% (reduced), INR 1.5 (elevated).

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of asterixis and disorientation confirms hepatic encephalopathy, indicating acute liver failure rather than just hepatitis. I need to determine if there is an underlying toxin causing this rapid decline, so have you recently taken any over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen Level, Coagulation Profile.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetaminophen Level: Not detected; Coagulation Profile: INR 1.5 (elevated), Prothrombin Time Activity < 40% (reduced).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative acetaminophen level and your history of high-risk sexual behavior, I need to confirm if a viral infection like Hepatitis B or A is the culprit. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen, Hepatitis A IgM, and Blood Alcohol Level.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hepatitis B Surface Antigen: Positive; Hepatitis A IgM: Negative; Blood Alcohol Level: 0.0 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your positive Hepatitis B Surface Antigen confirms an acute Hepatitis B infection, which explains your jaundice and liver failure. I will now review your liver imaging to assess for any complications before finalizing the treatment plan. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.
